explanation: Class template specialization in C++ allows developers to define custom implementations of a class template for specific template arguments. This feature enables optimized or specialized behavior when certain types are used, improving efficiency and flexibility in generic programming. Specializations can be full (completely defining behavior for specific types) or partial (specializing only some template parameters). It is essential for tailoring generic classes to particular use cases while maintaining code reuse.
example_explanation: This example demonstrates class template specialization by defining a generic template class 'MyContainer' and providing a full specialization for the 'int' type. When creating an object with 'double', the generic implementation is used, displaying 'Generic template'. When creating an object with 'int', the specialized version is invoked, displaying 'Specialized template for int'. This showcases how C++ allows customizing class behavior for specific types through specialization, a key feature for efficient and type-specific programming in modern C++.
